panel_intro: One question at a time — nothing here is submitted anywhere.

location.text: Is the vehicle currently stopped in a travel lane or another unsafe spot?

options.label: No, it's safely off the road

restart.text: Does the engine still start and run, even briefly?

options.label: No, it won't start at all
Yes, but it's clearly out of fuel

distance.text: Is a gas station within easy, safe walking distance?

unsafe_location.title: Move Only to Immediate Safety
unsafe_location.summary: Running low on fuel isn't urgent by itself, but an unsafe location is. If you can safely move a short distance — like onto the shoulder — do that first.
unsafe_location.confidence_text: Location safety always outranks the fuel question itself.
not_to_do: Don't attempt to walk for fuel from an unsafe travel lane.
Don't stand behind or beside the vehicle in traffic.
Don't try to restart the engine repeatedly while stopped in a live lane.
before_help_checklist: Turn on hazard lights before and after moving.
Check mirrors and traffic before moving at all.
Once safely stopped, exit on the side away from traffic.
Call roadside assistance once you're safely off the road.

phone_script.intro: Read this once you're safely stopped and calling for help.
lines: Hi, I'm out of fuel and now safely stopped at [location description].
Can you confirm ETA for fuel delivery?

unsafe_location.next_action: Once you're safely off the road, use this tool again if anything about the situation has changed.

possible_fuel_system.title: Call Roadside Assistance First
possible_fuel_system.summary: If the engine won't start at all, this may not be simple fuel exhaustion — a fuel pump or fuel system issue is possible. A technician can confirm on the spot rather than guessing.
possible_fuel_system.confidence_text: A total failure to start points away from ordinary fuel exhaustion, but only a technician can confirm the actual cause.
not_to_do: Don't assume adding fuel will fix it if the tank isn't actually empty.
Don't keep cranking the engine repeatedly.
Don't ignore any unusual sounds (whining, clicking) when you try to start it.
before_help_checklist: Note your fuel gauge reading before assuming it's empty.
Note any sounds when you try to start it.
Have your keys and vehicle location ready.
Stay with the vehicle if it's safe to do so.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with roadside assistance.
lines: Hi, my vehicle won't start and I'm not sure if it's out of fuel or something else. I'm at [location description].
Can you confirm ETA, and whether this sounds like a fuel system issue to you?

possible_fuel_system.next_action: If fuel wasn't the issue, ask the shop to check the fuel pump and fuel delivery system.

walk_to_station.title: Safe to Reassess — Walking Is Reasonable
walk_to_station.summary: If a station is genuinely close and the walk is safe (sidewalk or shoulder, good visibility, no highway crossing), getting a small amount of fuel yourself is often the fastest fix.
walk_to_station.confidence_text: This depends entirely on how safe the actual walk is — if it means crossing a highway or walking with no shoulder, call for fuel delivery instead.
not_to_do: Don't walk along a highway shoulder or cross active traffic to reach a station.
Don't carry fuel in anything other than an approved container.
Don't leave the vehicle in an unsafe spot while you're gone.
before_help_checklist: Turn on hazard lights before you leave.
Bring an approved fuel container if the station has one to lend or sell.
Lock the vehicle if you're stepping away.
Have a phone and a way to call for help if the walk turns out to be unsafe.

phone_script.intro: Keep this ready in case the walk doesn't work out.
lines: Hi, I'm out of fuel at [location description] and about to walk to a nearby station.
Can you confirm ETA for fuel delivery in case I need to call back?

walk_to_station.next_action: Keep an eye on your gauge going forward — running dry repeatedly can also damage a fuel pump over time.

fuel_delivery.title: Call Roadside Assistance First
fuel_delivery.summary: No station within safe walking distance means roadside fuel delivery is the practical next step.
fuel_delivery.confidence_text: This is a textbook roadside-assistance case.
not_to_do: Don't attempt a long or unsafe walk to find fuel yourself.
Don't keep cranking the engine trying to coax out the last fumes.
Don't forget some plans limit free fuel delivery to a small amount.
before_help_checklist: Pull as far off the road as safely possible.
Confirm your plan covers fuel delivery, not just towing.
Stay with the vehicle if it's safe to do so.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with roadside assistance.
lines: Hi, I've run out of fuel at [location description].
Can you confirm ETA and whether fuel delivery is included in my plan?

fuel_delivery.next_action: Keep an eye on your gauge going forward — running dry can also damage a fuel pump over time.
